environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: Two fresh servers, two runs each: the client sends the head, waits, and receives `eof` at exactly 2.00 s with an empty response (`hex=` empty, r0 and r1 identical). The `Expect: 100-continue` header is copied to the upstream verbatim by the `:97` loop but nothing in the proxy answers the contract, so a compliant client either times out or writes blindly into a socket the proxy is about to close.
findings.title: No `100 Continue` is ever synthesised, so a client that correctly waits for it is closed with zero bytes after 2 s

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line
